reason: S1 adds a required caller-controlled float fill_weight parameter to meshopt_buildMeshletsSplit, but H0 still invokes the function with the old arity and therefore does not exercise the new parameter. This is both an API compatibility gap and a material fuzzing gap because fill_weight changes the cluster-selection tradeoff between maximum fill and SAH quality.
evidence: In src/meshoptimizer.h and src/clusterizer.cpp, meshopt_buildMeshletsSplit gains a final float fill_weight parameter.
The header states that fill_weight prioritizes clusters closer to maximum size at some cost to SAH quality and identifies 0.5 as a safe default.
S1 production callers demonstrate distinct configurations: demo/main.cpp passes 0.f while demo/nanite.cpp passes split_weight initialized to 0.5f.
All six meshopt_buildMeshletsSplit calls in tools/clusterfuzz.cpp end at max_triangles and supply no fill_weight argument.
The templated meshopt_buildMeshletsSplit<T> forwards fill_weight to the underlying function, exposing the same new input semantics.
recommended_action: Update every H0 call to the S1 signature and derive fill_weight from fuzz input, explicitly covering at least 0.f and 0.5f plus varied finite values and floating-point edge cases permitted by the API; retain multiple max_vertices/min_triangles/max_triangles combinations so interactions with fill_weight are exercised.
